[[File:Mrzezyno Artemisia campestris littoral sprout 2010.jpg|thumb|right|''Artemisia campestris'' near the [[Baltic Sea]]]]

'''''Artemisia campestris''''' is a common and widespread species of plants in the sunflower family, [[Asteraceae]]. It is native to a wide region of [[Eurasia]] and [[North America]].<ref name="eadt 2021">{{Cite web|last=Hill|first=Chris|date=2021-02-03|title='Incredibly rare' plants burst into life on busy industrial estate|url=https://www.eadt.co.uk/news/field-wormwood-thrives-at-brandon-industrial-estate-7302138|access-date=2021-02-05|website=East Anglian Daily Times|language=en-UK}}</ref> Common names include '''field wormwood''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17}}</ref> '''beach wormwood''',<ref>{{Illinois Wildflowers |prairie|plantx|beach_ww|Beach Wormwood (Artemisia campestris caudata)}}</ref> '''northern wormwood''',<ref>[http://oregon.gov/ODA/PLANT/CONSERVATION/profile_arcawo.shtml Second alternative name]</ref> '''Breckland wormwood''',<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.buglife.org.uk/discoverbugs/bugofthemonth/The+Wormwood+moonshiner |title=3rd alternative name |access-date=2012-02-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120409162835/http://www.buglife.org.uk/discoverbugs/bugofthemonth/The+Wormwood+moonshiner |archive-date=2012-04-09 |url-status=dead }}</ref> '''boreal wormwood''', '''Canadian wormwood''', '''field sagewort''' and '''field mugwort.'''<ref name=h>{{eFloras|1|200023184|Artemisia campestris |first=Leila M. |last=Shultz |family=Anthemideae}}</ref><ref name=w>{{eFloras|2|200023184|Artemisia campestris |first1=Yourun |last1=Lin |first2=Christopher J. |last2=Humphries |first3=Michael G. |last3=Gilbert |family=Asteraceae}}</ref><ref name=p>[http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/index1.php?scientific-name=artemisia+campestris Altervista Flora Italiana, Assenzio di campo, ''Artemisia campestris'' L.]</ref>

''Artemisia campestris'' is a branching, [[aromatic]] plant up to {{cvt|150|cm|ft|0}} tall. It grows in open sites on dry sandy soils, in [[steppes]], rocky slopes, and waste areas.<ref name=w/>
